study.question: Can objective-specific learning at the shared residual task-scorer boundary improve the combined memory/task model beyond incumbent macro AUC 0.8310755947860231, and which task groups supply useful upstream learning under the frozen protocol?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: R12 private/linear beats g0 by 0.0006966769079054 macro AUC, but click AUC changes -0.0000803863458994 while cart/fav improve +0.0013664593678040/+0.0014729427568423. This does not measure interference. Private routing beats mean at linear and copy bases; their single-seed interaction is +0.0003554657336956. R13 memory-context/private and static-context/private score 0.8309696093096159 and 0.8309294998382515, both below R12; contextual enrichment is not supported by these implementations. Hypothesis: tasks benefit from private forward summaries, while click-driven upstream adaptation of their common scorer trunk may reduce auxiliary utility. Blocking only the click hidden-to-head backward edge may improve the macro objective with identical forward capacity. The competing hypothesis is that all task gradients are useful; a matched 2x2 tests both. This is a path-utility hypothesis, not an assertion that conflicts have been observed.

study.proposed_difference: A 2x2 factorial controls click/auxiliary access to the shared residual scorer hidden output. Each selected task head receives hidden.detach(); its head parameters still train and its forward values are unchanged. Unselected heads receive hidden. The trunk is evaluated once in every arm, preserving Dice forward updates. This boundary jointly stops scorer-path upstream gradients to trunk and its embedding inputs, not the task loss globally. Four standalone modules implement click-only stop (candidate), all-open replay, auxiliary-only stop and both-stop. Both-stop keeps trunk parameters at initialization but running Dice statistics active. No architectural novelty, performance gain or gradient-conflict measurement is claimed before host evaluation.
predictions: At any common state, every arm has identical four prediction probabilities and sum-BCE forward value for the same batch, FP32/BF16 precision and mode. Initial states and CPU RNG match R12 exactly; all-open gradients match R12.

After opening zero-initialized final scorer layers in a diagnostic clone, a click-only loss contributes no gradient through the shared scorer hidden boundary when click-stop is true; analogous auxiliary tests follow their flag. Head gradients, projected-value path and other inherited routes remain live where inputs are nondegenerate.

Directional prediction: click-only stop improves validation macro AUC over all-open while retaining useful auxiliary scorer learning; auxiliary-only and both-stop do not reproduce the full benefit. This is unmeasured and may fail.

Parameter total remains 33069257, embedding31793216, dense1276041. Forward operator structure and inference cost should remain close to R12; backward work can decline. Measure actual training/wall/inference cost and peak memory rather than claiming equal compute.

Selection uses all four task AUCs equally with the frozen loss/parameter/ID tie breakers. Record each task AUC/Logloss and deltas against DIN, g0, g3 and R12; explain any click or auxiliary regression without introducing a task veto.
falsifiers: If common-state predictions, Dice updates, parameter shapes or initial states differ beyond inherited numerical tolerances across flags, the implementation fails the matched-forward claim and cannot answer the question.
If isolated nondegenerate head-loss probes cross the blocked hidden boundary, or if blocking unintentionally removes head/value learning, reject the implementation and retain all failed costs.
If click-only stop fails to improve macro AUC against a faithful all-open replay, the proposed directional benefit is unsupported in this implementation.

If both-stop matches or exceeds click-only stop, or auxiliary-only stop wins, do not attribute an improvement specifically to removal of click interference; fixed random features, regularization, alternate task dominance or clipping changes remain plausible.
If a small gain disappears or reverses over paired seeds, retain a preliminary/null conclusion. One seed and repeated validation comparisons do not establish mechanism or significance.
alternative_explanations: One seed and validation reuse cannot establish significance or generalization; no task-gradient norms or conflict measurements have yet been recorded.
Stopping at hidden jointly removes that objective path into shared trunk parameters, trunk Dice alpha and score-input embeddings; it does not isolate those components.
Every task still updates direct value embeddings and other inherited paths. These indirect shared updates prevent claiming complete objective isolation.
The both-blocked arm leaves scorer-trunk parameters without task gradients; Dice running statistics still evolve. Effective learned capacity and frozen-optimizer treatment differ by design.
Gradient clipping uses a global dense norm, so removal of a path can change scaling of other dense gradients. Weight decay/skipped-gradient behavior and backward cost require host measurement.

The original improvement may arise from capacity or a private readout alone; R12 mean/copy factorial only partly addresses this. A gradient-only suite cannot establish memory/task synergy independent of their shared ancestry.
R13 context controls show small/no gains, not a refutation of all context conditioning; scorer initialization, limited single-pass adaptation or context compression could explain their null results.

No failed execution is present among the authorized committed records; R12 mean/copy and R13 mean-context are unsuccessful predictive branches, not runtime failures. Retain their receipts and costs. No closed assessment archive, external campaign or personal source is an input.
